item.title: The Bolsonaros…they’re back! Brazil heads to the polls – podcast
item.description: Brazil held its first-round presidential election on Sunday. Flávio Bolsonaro, son of the jailed former president, ran to succeed his father. Jair Bolsonaro was convicted in September 2025 of attempting a coup. The campaign tested whether his political legacy survived the conviction. The Bolsonarosthey’re back! Brazil heads to the polls – podcast.

item.description: The comments came after Seoul’s ​military and the ‌UN Command said North Korea violated the Korean War armistice following a landmine blast last week that wounded three South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized ‌Zone (DMZ). South Korea's Lee urges North Korea to restore dialogue, pledges military buildup.

item.title: Kyrgyz Activist Gets 2 Years For Criticizing Growing Chinese Presence
item.description: The Lenin District Court in Bishkek found activist and politician Mavlyan Askarbekov guilty and sentenced to two years in prison on offenses related to a law on incitement of racial, ethnic, national, religious, or interregional hatred, a verdict he called "absurd." Kyrgyz Activist Gets 2 Years For Criticizing Growing Chinese Presence.

item.title: Turkiye detains suspect in 2013 attack by Syria border: report
item.description: Turkiye arrested Omar al‑Khatib, a Syrian linked to a 2013 border attack, after an Interpol red notice surfaced. Authorities say he coordinated attackers with intelligence officials loyal to former president Bashar Omar al-Khatib, a Syrian who was the subject of an Interpol red notice, is believed to have coordinated between the attackers and intelligence officials loyal to Syria's then president Bashar al-Assad, Anadolu news agency reported.

item.title: Blasts in Ethiopian capital after government banned drone flights
item.description: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed is due to be sworn in for a new term on Monday after winning elections in June, but faces conflict on multiple fronts as several armed groups have formed an alliance against him. Blasts in Ethiopian capital after government banned drone flights.

item.title: Oil Exports Find A Way Past Iranian Attacks, But Refinery Bottleneck Persists
item.description: Exports of crude oil from the Middle East hit their highest level in September since the war with Iran began, reinforcing a trend of increased supplies despite Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, according to analysis of shipping and commodity market data by industry observers. Oil Exports Find A Way Past Iranian Attacks, But Refinery Bottleneck Persists.

item.title: Georgia Summons Iranian Ambassador Over Remarks On Revered Queen Ketevan
item.description: Georgia summoned Iran’s ambassador after his planned book Georgia has summoned Iran’s ambassador after his plans to publish a personal interpretation of Queen Ketevan’s history sparked criticism from ruling party lawmakers. Revered as a saint in Georgia, Ketevan was tortured and killed in Persia in the 17th century after refusing to renounce Christianity. Georgia Summons Iranian Ambassador Over Remarks On Revered Queen Ketevan.

item.title: Afghanistan’s TTP sanctuary is becoming harder to deny
item.description: For years, Pakistan’s claim that the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan operates from sanctuaries inside Afghanistan produced a familiar exchange: Islamabad accused, Kabul denied, and each new militant attack triggered another round of recrimination. That pattern is becoming harder to sustain. The sanctuary dispute can now be tested against a growing body of evidence rather than competing claims [] The p Afghanistan’s TTP sanctuary is becoming harder to deny.

item.title: Ebola response faces setback as transit centre burns down in DR Congo camp
item.description: The enormous challenge of halting the spread of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) just became even harder after a key transit centre for patients requiring treatment burned down in Ituri province. Ebola response faces setback as transit centre burns down in DR Congo camp.

item.title: Nepal floods threaten jobs and livelihoods beyond disaster zone: ILO
item.description: The deadly flash floods in northern Nepal have severely disrupted employment and livelihoods, with wider impacts beyond communities that were directly affected, the International Labour Organization (ILO) said in a preliminary assessment released on Thursday. Nepal floods threaten jobs and livelihoods beyond disaster zone: ILO.

item.title: 'Exhausted' Afghan Refugees Get Extension At Camp In Qatar As US Lawmakers Urge Action
item.description: Qatar will keep the Afghan refugee camp open for another nine months after the closure deadline passed, according to Afghan refugees being held at a camp in Qatar have been told it will be kept open for another nine months after a deadline for its closure passed, but they face continuing uncertainty over their fate amid an ongoing bar on entry to the United States.

item.title: Ukraine Delivers Food By Drone As Russian-Occupied Oleshky Faces Starvation
item.description: Oleshky, a Ukrainian city occupied by Russian forces 9 kilometers from Kherson, is on the brink of a humanitarian catastrophe. Since 2023, the city has been without electricity, gas, or drinking water. Now, Ukrainian teams are airlifting food supplies into the embattled area. Ukraine Delivers Food By Drone As Russian-Occupied Oleshky Faces Starvation.

item.description: President announces measures amid anger at authorities over recent murders of womenSouth Africa’s president has called on men to take more responsibility for violence against women as he announced measures to tackle the problem, amid anger at authorities over a recent wave of murders.
